statement: Align one or more elements to a picked reference such as a wall face, grid, plane or edge, with optional lock.
superiority: Align multiple element types at once with a visible target preview.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: After align, element face lies within 1e-3 mm of the target and a lock keeps it there after edits.

statement: Copy or move a line, wall, beam or edge by a distance, in a chosen direction, by graphical or numeric entry.

source.ref: Move or Copy Elements with the Offset Tool

superiority: Support offset chains with corner treatment and live preview.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Offset of a 5 m line by 300 mm gives a parallel copy at exactly 300 mm.

statement: Mirror selected elements about a picked line or plane, with optional copy.
superiority: Preview the mirror before commit and mirror hosted relationships.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Mirrored element equals the reflection of the original about the axis.

statement: Mirror selected elements about a line drawn on the fly.
superiority: Same, with snap to datums.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Mirror about drawn line produces the reflected geometry.

statement: Move selected elements by a specified displacement with optional constrain and disjoin.

source.ref: Move Elements with the Move Tool

superiority: Show before-and-after ghost and keep joins healthy.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Moved element displacement equals the entered vector.

statement: Copy selected elements by displacement, with Multiple, Constrain and base-point options.

source.ref: Copy Elements with the Copy Tool

superiority: Copy to levels in one step with relationships preserved.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Copy offset equals input and count equals clicks.

statement: Rotate selected elements around a centre by an angle with optional copy.
superiority: Rotate with angle snaps and live preview of dependent elements.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Rotating a point by 90 degrees around the centre matches the rotation matrix.

statement: Trim or extend two elements to form a corner.
superiority: Preview result and accept for multiple pairs in a row.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Two lines meet at their intersection point.

statement: Trim or extend one element to meet a boundary element picked second.
superiority: Show a preview of the result and accept several pairs in sequence.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: The trimmed element end lies on the boundary within 1e-6 mm.

statement: Trim or extend several elements to one boundary in one pass using a selection of elements.
superiority: Select elements with a fence and preview the result for the whole set.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: All selected element ends lie on the boundary after the command.

statement: Split a wall, beam or line into two at a point.
superiority: Split at several points in one command.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Resulting lengths sum to the original.

statement: Split a wall, pipe, duct, cable tray, conduit, toposolid, beam or column into two independent pieces separated by a user-set joint gap, e.g. for precast wall panels.

source.ref: Split Elements with a Defined Gap

superiority: Preview the gap and keep openings aligned.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Page lists walls, MEP runs, toposolids, framing and columns; detail/model lines are not listed, and the gap has a limited allowed range. Acceptance sketch: The gap equals the entered width and the two parts sum to the original less the gap.

statement: Create linear arrays with number, spacing, group-and-associate and constrain options.
superiority: Parametric array that updates numbers live.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Array with 5 copies at 600 mm spacing places elements at k*600.

statement: Create radial arrays with a centre, angle and count.
superiority: Edit centre and count by drag.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Copies at k*delta around centre.

statement: Scale selected elements about an origin, graphical or numeric.
superiority: Limit to supported element types with clear explanation.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Scaled length equals ratio times original.

statement: Pin elements to prevent accidental movement and unpin later.

source.ref: Use Pins to Lock Elements in Place

superiority: Pin state visible in properties and canvas.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Pinned element cannot be moved.

statement: Remove the selected elements from the model without copying them to the clipboard.
superiority: Show dependency impact preview before deleting.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Page documents Delete as plain removal that bypasses the clipboard; dependent-element warnings are not described there. Acceptance sketch: Dependent items listed in warning.

statement: Copy the type of one element to others with the paintbrush.

source.ref: Change Element Types Using the Match Type Tool

superiority: Match any property class with undo.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Target elements adopt the source type.

statement: Start placing another element of the same type as the selection.

source.ref: Copy Elements with the Create Similar Tool

superiority: One-click from any element.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Tool starts with the selected type.

statement: Copy elements and paste to the same place, current view, selected levels, selected views or a picked level.
superiority: Paste with preview of destination alignment.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Paste aligned to selected levels creates one copy per level at the same relative position.

statement: Create a parametric cope on intersecting steel beams so one member is notched around the other, with an associated connection shown at fine detail level.

source.ref: Cope Steel Framing Elements for Steel Fabrication

superiority: Auto-cope all framing joints in a selection.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Documented Cope tool lives on the Steel tab (Parametric Cuts panel), not the Modify tab, and is for steel fabrication detailing. Acceptance sketch: Removed cope area equals the intersection area in the section.

statement: Remove a join between two elements so their faces are distinct again.
superiority: Show join relationships in an overlay for quick unjoin.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: The shared edge reappears in section after unjoin.

statement: Reverse which element dominates a geometry join so the other cuts through.
superiority: Display the join order graph for a selection.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: After the switch the previously cut element takes precedence.

statement: Paint a material onto a face of an element without altering its type.

source.ref: Apply a Material to the Face of an Element

superiority: Paint with live preview and layer-aware limits.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Painted face reports the new material in schedules.

statement: Split a face of an element into regions so different materials can be painted on each.
superiority: Split by drawing on the face with snap to edges and show areas live.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Region areas sum to the original face area.

statement: Group selected elements to reuse and edit together.

source.ref: Create a Group by Selecting Elements

superiority: Nested group edit with diffs.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Group instances move together.

statement: Ungroup a group to edit its members individually, open the group to add or remove members, or edit the group in its own file and reload it into projects.
superiority: Show instance diffs and allow per-instance overrides.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Ungroup and Edit Group are documented together; external editing and reload are on the Edit a Group Externally page, and 'save as a separate file' is not described on this page. Acceptance sketch: Editing a group member updates every group instance.

statement: Combine selected elements into a named assembly type listed in the project browser, from which assembly views, schedules and sheets can then be generated.
superiority: Auto-generate fabrication sheets from assembly templates.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Create Assembly only builds the assembly; views and sheets come from a separate command (Create Assembly Views and Sheets). Acceptance sketch: Assembly gets its own set of views and a parts list schedule.

statement: Divide layered elements into parts that can be scheduled and detailed separately.
superiority: Slice parts by rule and keep them linked to the host.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Sum of part volumes equals the host layer volume.

statement: Select all instances of a type in the view or project.
superiority: Include query by parameter.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Count equals number of instances.

statement: Lock or unlock element relationships such as alignments and equal dimensions.
superiority: Display a constraint overlay to see locked relationships.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: A locked alignment holds after moving the reference.

statement: Open the family of the selected instance in the family editor and reload on save.
superiority: Edit a family live in context with immediate project updates.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Edited family reloads into the project and updates all instances.

statement: Flip orientation or hand of elements such as doors, walls and stairs using flip arrows.
superiority: Show flip arrows consistently and support multi-selection flip.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Flipping twice returns the original orientation.

statement: Measure distance between two references without placing a dimension.
superiority: Keep several measurements pinned and exportable.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Measured value equals the analytic distance within display precision.

statement: Rotate a custom fill pattern while defining it and save the result as a new rotated pattern type.
superiority: Preview the rotated pattern at several scales.
notes: ADDED 2026-11-14: Revit 2027 What’s New feature with no matching row in the original register Acceptance sketch: Rotate a hatch by 30 degrees and verify the saved pattern lines run at that angle.
